source.title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN - AWS Documentation
source.applicability: Official configuration documentation for establishing secure network connectivity between AWS VPCs and on-premises networks. Implements routing rules, traffic segmentation, and security group integration required by the network boundary and remote access components of the scope.

passages.text: By default, an instance that you launch within an Amazon VPC can't communicate with a local (AWS Cloud) network and a remote device — for example, this might be a site or an on-premises device. You can enable access to your remote devices from your VPC by creating an AWS Site-to-Site VPN (Site-to-Site VPN) connection, and configuring routing to pass traffic through the connection.
Each VPN connection includes two VPN tunnels which you can simultaneously use for high availability.

What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?




By default, an instance that you launch within an Amazon VPC can't communicate with a local
        (AWS Cloud) network and a remote device — for example, this might be a site or an
        on-premises device. You can enable access to your remote devices from your VPC by creating
        an AWS Site-to-Site VPN (Site-to-Site VPN) connection, and configuring routing to pass traffic through the
        connection.
